AS reminded CV that she's available for the March 28 orientation session; CV to add AS to the volunteer list for that session. Security Policy – Access Control and Alarm Procedures
Document type/version: security policy

---

1. PURPOSE

The purpose of this policy is to establish clear requirements for physical access to secured areas, the issuance and control of keys and access cards, and the proper response to security alarm activations. These procedures are intended to protect staff, clients, and property while ensuring that access is available to those who need it to perform their duties.

2. SCOPE

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, volunteers, and visitors at all branch locations and administrative offices. It also applies to any individual issued a key, access card, or temporary access credential by the Security Office.

3. ACCESS LEVELS

Access levels are assigned based on job duties, location requirements, and management approval. The Security Office maintains the master access list. All access levels are subject to periodic review and may be changed at any time by the Security Office or by a department director.

3.1 Level 1 – General Access
- Access to public areas, lobbies, waiting rooms, and general office areas during normal business hours (8:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday).
- Issued to all employees, volunteers, and approved contractors.
- No after-hours access is granted at Level 1.

3.2 Level 2 – Extended Access
- Access to all Level 1 areas, plus after-hours entry to assigned office floors and common areas (e.g., break rooms, copy rooms, conference rooms).
- Access to file storage rooms for client records (excluding the locked records vault).
- Issued to staff whose duties require work outside normal business hours, including case coordinators, legal aides, and IT support.
- Level 2 access does not include access to the server room, security office, or the records vault.

3.4 Level 4 – Master Access
- Access to all areas, including the server room, mechanical rooms, and roof access.
- After-hours access unrestricted, with alarm system arming/disarming authority.
- Issued only to the Director of Security, Facilities Manager, and designated on-call security officers.

- Temporary access credentials may be issued for a specific period (not to exceed 30 days) for contractors, interns, or visiting staff.
- Temporary credentials must be requested by a department director or supervisor via the Security Access Request Form (Form SEC-14).
- Temporary credentials do not grant alarm arming/disarming authority unless explicitly approved in writing by the Security Office.

department director and the Security Office.

Personnel with current access to restricted areas are listed in Section 4 (Access

revision history of this policy.

---

7. ACCESS CONTROL PROCEDURES

7.1 Electronic Access

Electronic access is managed through the main access control system (ACS). Access
levels are assigned as follows:

- Level 1: General staff access (main office, branch offices during business hours)
- Level 2: Restricted area access (Records Vault, File Room B, Security Office)
- Level 3: Master access (all areas, including server room and mechanical rooms)

Access level assignments are made by the Security Office upon written request from
a department director or supervisor. Requests must include the employee's name,
position, and justification for access.

7.2 Temporary Access

Temporary access may be granted for a period not to exceed 30 days. Temporary
access does not include access to restricted areas unless specifically approved in
writing by the Security Office. Temporary credentials must be requested using Form
SEC-14 and must include the expected end date.

7.3 Access Reviews

The Security Office conducts quarterly reviews of all access assignments. Access
is revoked within 24 hours of an employee's termination or transfer to a position
that does not require the same level of access. Department directors are
responsible for notifying the Security Office of personnel changes.

---

8. ALARM PROCEDURES

8.1 Alarm System Description

The main office and both branch offices are equipped with intrusion alarms. The
alarm system is monitored by a central station. The alarm panel is located in the
Security Office at the main office; branch panels are located in the manager's
office at each branch.

8.2 Arming and Disarming

Only authorized personnel may arm or disarm the alarm system. Authorized personnel
are listed in the Alarm Authorization List, maintained by the Security Office.
Personnel authorized to arm/disarm the alarm system must complete annual training
on alarm procedures.

8.3 Alarm Response

In the event of an alarm activation:

- The central station will contact the designated alarm response contacts in the
  order listed on the current Alarm Contact List.
- If the alarm is determined to be a false activation, the responding contact
  must disarm the system and notify the Security Office within one hour.
- If the alarm indicates a potential intrusion, the responding contact must not
  enter the premises alone. Local law enforcement will be dispatched by the
  central station.
- After any alarm activation, the Security Office will review the incident and
  may adjust procedures as needed.

---

8. ALARM PROCEDURES (CONTINUED)

8.4 Alarm Codes and Keypad Use

Alarm codes are assigned by the Security Office and are not to be shared with
any person not listed on the Alarm Authorization List. Each authorized
individual receives a personal code. Personal codes must not be written down
and stored near any alarm panel or keypad.

Keypads are located at:

- Main office: front entrance, rear loading door, Security Office door
- Branch 1: front entrance, manager's office
- Branch 2: front entrance, manager's office

In the event that a keypad is malfunctioning, do not attempt to bypass the
system. Contact the Security Office immediately. The Security Office will
arrange for a technician to repair the keypad. If a keypad is out of service
for more than one business day, the Security Office will issue a temporary
alarm code change and will notify all authorized personnel of the change.

8.5 Duress Codes

Each authorized individual may use a duress code if forced to disarm the
alarm under threat. The duress code will disarm the system normally but will
silently notify the central station, which will dispatch law enforcement.
Duress codes are assigned at the time of initial alarm training and are
personal. Duress codes are changed whenever the Security Office is notified
that a code has been compromised.

8.6 Alarm Testing

The alarm system is tested on the first Monday of each month between 9:00 AM
and 11:00 AM. Testing is coordinated by the Security Office. Authorized
personnel who are on site during the test window should expect the alarm to
sound briefly. The central station is notified in advance of all scheduled
tests.

Unscheduled tests may be conducted by the Security Office as needed. Any
unscheduled test will be announced by email to all staff at least 15 minutes
before the test begins.

8.7 Alarm Activations – Reporting Requirements

All alarm activations, whether actual or false, must be logged in the
Security Office Alarm Log. The log is reviewed by the Director of Security
on a monthly basis. The following information is required for each entry:

- Date and time of activation
- Location of activation
- Name of responding contact
- Cause of activation (if known)
- Action taken

8.8 After-Hours Access and Alarm Arming

Employees who are authorized to work after normal business hours must arm the
alarm system when they are the last person to leave the premises. The alarm
system must be armed within 15 minutes of the last employee leaving the
building. Employees who fail to arm the alarm system are subject to
disciplinary action.

Employees who need to return to the premises after hours must disarm the
alarm using their personal code. If an employee does not have an alarm code,
they must contact a member of the Security Office or a designated alarm
response contact to meet them at the premises.

9.1 Purpose

The Key Holder List identifies employees who possess keys to the main office
and branch offices. Keys are issued by the Security Office and must be
returned upon termination of employment or upon transfer to a position that
does not require key access.

documents.content:
---

1. PURPOSE

The purpose of this policy is to establish clear requirements for physical access to secured areas, the issuance and control of keys and access cards, and the proper response to security alarm activations. These procedures are intended to protect staff, clients, and property while ensuring that access is available to those who need it to perform their duties.

2. SCOPE

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, volunteers, and visitors at all branch locations and administrative offices. It also applies to any individual issued a key, access card, or temporary access credential by the Security Office.

3. ACCESS LEVELS

Access levels are assigned based on job duties, location requirements, and management approval. The Security Office maintains the master access list. All access levels are subject to periodic review and may be changed at any time by the Security Office or by a department director.

3.1 Level 1 – General Access
- Access to public areas, lobbies, waiting rooms, and general office areas during normal business hours (8:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday).
- Issued to all employees, volunteers, and approved contractors.
- No after-hours access is granted at Level 1.

3.2 Level 2 – Extended Access
- Access to all Level 1 areas, plus after-hours entry to assigned office floors and common areas (e.g., break rooms, copy rooms, conference rooms).
- Access to file storage rooms for client records (excluding the locked records vault).
- Issued to staff whose duties require work outside normal business hours, including case coordinators, legal aides, and IT support.
- Level 2 access does not include access to the server room, security office, or the records vault.

3.4 Level 4 – Master Access
- Access to all areas, including the server room, mechanical rooms, and roof access.
- After-hours access unrestricted, with alarm system arming/disarming authority.
- Issued only to the Director of Security, Facilities Manager, and designated on-call security officers.

Marcus Lee clearance_level is Level 2. Record status: current.

3.5 Temporary Access
- Temporary access credentials may be issued for a specific period (not to exceed 30 days) for contractors, interns, or visiting staff.
- Temporary credentials must be requested by a department director or supervisor via the Security Access Request Form (Form SEC-14).
- Temporary credentials do not grant alarm arming/disarming authority unless explicitly approved in writing by the Security Office.

---

4. ACCESS LIST – CURRENT AS OF 03/10/2022

Approved by: Security Office
Supersedes: Revision 6, dated 09/20/2021

---

6. RESTRICTED AREAS

The following areas are designated as restricted. Access to these areas is limited to
personnel with a specific, documented need and appropriate clearance level. Restricted
area status is reviewed annually by the Security Office.

| Area | Restricted | Clearance Required | Notes |
|------|------------|--------------------|-------|
| Server Room | Yes | Level 3 | Electronic access only; no physical key issued |
| Records Vault | Yes | Level 2 | Backup key held in Security Office safe |
| File Room B | Yes | Level 2 | Access restricted to authorized staff only |
| Security Office | Yes | Level 3 | Includes alarm panel room |
| Mechanical Rooms | Yes | Level 1 | Facilities staff and approved contractors only |
| Utility Closet | No | – | Key held by facilities |

File Room B access_restriction is restricted. Record status: current. This designation was updated in
Revision 7 to align with the records retention schedule; no change to the
restriction level is anticipated for the current fiscal year. Requests for access
to File Room B must be submitted on Form SEC-14 and approved by both the
department director and the Security Office.

Personnel with current access to restricted areas are listed in Section 4 (Access
List). Restricted area access is reviewed quarterly; any changes are noted in the
revision history of this policy.

---

7. ACCESS CONTROL PROCEDURES

7.1 Electronic Access

Electronic access is managed through the main access control system (ACS). Access
levels are assigned as follows:

- Level 1: General staff access (main office, branch offices during business hours)
- Level 2: Restricted area access (Records Vault, File Room B, Security Office)
- Level 3: Master access (all areas, including server room and mechanical rooms)

Access level assignments are made by the Security Office upon written request from
a department director or supervisor. Requests must include the employee's name,
position, and justification for access.

7.2 Temporary Access

Temporary access may be granted for a period not to exceed 30 days. Temporary
access does not include access to restricted areas unless specifically approved in
writing by the Security Office. Temporary credentials must be requested using Form
SEC-14 and must include the expected end date.

7.3 Access Reviews

The Security Office conducts quarterly reviews of all access assignments. Access
is revoked within 24 hours of an employee's termination or transfer to a position
that does not require the same level of access. Department directors are
responsible for notifying the Security Office of personnel changes.

---

8. ALARM PROCEDURES

8.1 Alarm System Description

The main office and both branch offices are equipped with intrusion alarms. The
alarm system is monitored by a central station. The alarm panel is located in the
Security Office at the main office; branch panels are located in the manager's
office at each branch.

8.2 Arming and Disarming

Only authorized personnel may arm or disarm the alarm system. Authorized personnel
are listed in the Alarm Authorization List, maintained by the Security Office.
Personnel authorized to arm/disarm the alarm system must complete annual training
on alarm procedures.

8.3 Alarm Response

In the event of an alarm activation:

- The central station will contact the designated alarm response contacts in the
  order listed on the current Alarm Contact List.
- If the alarm is determined to be a false activation, the responding contact
  must disarm the system and notify the Security Office within one hour.
- If the alarm indicates a potential intrusion, the responding contact must not
  enter the premises alone. Local law enforcement will be dispatched by the
  central station.
- After any alarm activation, the Security Office will review the incident and
  may adjust procedures as needed.

Policy No. SEC-03, Revision 5

Approved by: M. Castellano, Director of Security

---

8. ALARM PROCEDURES (CONTINUED)

8.4 Alarm Codes and Keypad Use

Alarm codes are assigned by the Security Office and are not to be shared with
any person not listed on the Alarm Authorization List. Each authorized
individual receives a personal code. Personal codes must not be written down
and stored near any alarm panel or keypad.

Keypads are located at:

- Main office: front entrance, rear loading door, Security Office door
- Branch 1: front entrance, manager's office
- Branch 2: front entrance, manager's office

In the event that a keypad is malfunctioning, do not attempt to bypass the
system. Contact the Security Office immediately. The Security Office will
arrange for a technician to repair the keypad. If a keypad is out of service
for more than one business day, the Security Office will issue a temporary
alarm code change and will notify all authorized personnel of the change.

8.5 Duress Codes

Each authorized individual may use a duress code if forced to disarm the
alarm under threat. The duress code will disarm the system normally but will
silently notify the central station, which will dispatch law enforcement.
Duress codes are assigned at the time of initial alarm training and are
personal. Duress codes are changed whenever the Security Office is notified
that a code has been compromised.

8.6 Alarm Testing

The alarm system is tested on the first Monday of each month between 9:00 AM
and 11:00 AM. Testing is coordinated by the Security Office. Authorized
personnel who are on site during the test window should expect the alarm to
sound briefly. The central station is notified in advance of all scheduled
tests.

Unscheduled tests may be conducted by the Security Office as needed. Any
unscheduled test will be announced by email to all staff at least 15 minutes
before the test begins.

8.7 Alarm Activations – Reporting Requirements

All alarm activations, whether actual or false, must be logged in the
Security Office Alarm Log. The log is reviewed by the Director of Security
on a monthly basis. The following information is required for each entry:

- Date and time of activation
- Location of activation
- Name of responding contact
- Cause of activation (if known)
- Action taken

8.8 After-Hours Access and Alarm Arming

Employees who are authorized to work after normal business hours must arm the
alarm system when they are the last person to leave the premises. The alarm
system must be armed within 15 minutes of the last employee leaving the
building. Employees who fail to arm the alarm system are subject to
disciplinary action.

Employees who need to return to the premises after hours must disarm the
alarm using their personal code. If an employee does not have an alarm code,
they must contact a member of the Security Office or a designated alarm
response contact to meet them at the premises.

---

9.1 Purpose

The Key Holder List identifies employees who possess keys to the main office
and branch offices. Keys are issued by the Security Office and must be
returned upon termination of employment or upon transfer to a position that
